Walmart announces it will officially launch Apple Pay support next week. The retailer resisted offering Apple Pay support for over a decade under consumer pressure.

Apple Pay finally lands at Walmart

Walmart announced today in a press release that contactless payment features, including Apple Pay, will be rolled out at select Walmart and Sam's Club stores starting August 24. The feature will cover all U.S. locations by the end of this year and expand to fuel stations by mid-2027.

Walmart is adding full contactless payment support, which includes Apple Pay on iPhone and Apple Watch, Google Pay, contactless credit cards, and other payment platforms. Consumers can also add Walmart and Sam's Club membership cards to platforms like Apple Wallet. Contactless payment will operate alongside existing payment methods, including Walmart's own Walmart Pay.

The company stated:

Walmart is one of the last major retailers to refuse Apple Pay support, making this a huge win for consumers. For years, the retailer had refused to offer contactless payment, sticking with its QR code-based payment system, Walmart Pay.

As recently as last year, Walmart still firmly believed that Walmart Pay was more convenient for consumers than Apple Pay. However, to use Walmart Pay, users had to first add a credit or debit card to the Walmart app on their iPhone, then scan a QR code at checkout to pay.

A quick search on social media reveals just how frustrated users have been about Walmart's refusal to support Apple Pay.

After all, other retailers that long refused Apple Pay have already caved years ago, including Kroger, Home Depot, and H-E-B, each for their own reasons.

Has Walmart's lack of Apple Pay support affected your shopping habits? Now that Walmart and Sam's Club are getting Apple Pay, will you be more inclined to shop there? Let us know in the comments.
